q: The present study deliberately does not benchmark agent performance
r: IC1: source-code architectural taxonomy of agent scaffolds, no evaluation or comparison of agents on development tasks and no SDD or context files.

q: It does not benchmark or rank; it describes and compares how the systems are built.
r: IC1: source-code anatomy of coding harness architecture, not an evaluation of agents on tasks nor SDD or context mechanisms as studied variable.

q: A general assistant benchmark requiring web browsing, file manipulation, and multi-step reasoning.
r: IC1: general agent reliability on GAIA and tau-bench, not software development.

q: Research simple factual information from Wikipedia and pro- vide accurate answers to straightforward questions.
r: EC6: task suite mixes non-development tasks (research, multiple choice, ML and cyber tasks) so evaluated task is not clearly code development.

q: This MLR presents the current state of research on LLM–based multi-agent systems for code generation from both academic and industrial perspectives.
r: Include: 2025-26 multivocal review of multi-agent coding systems, their benchmarks, models and challenges (secondary study, RQ2-RQ3).

q: We build a novel benchmark named CAASD for objectively assessing the capabilities of various AI-aided software development systems.
r: Include: LLM framework with use-case and design artefacts building whole systems, new project-level benchmark compared with baselines on pass rate and tokens, 2024.

q: We introduce SWE-Lancer, a benchmark of over 1,400 freelance software engineering tasks from Upwork, valued at $1 million USD total in realworld payouts.
r: Include: new evaluation method (payout metric, e2e tests) for feature and bug tasks, not pure SWE-bench issue repair; contribution is the evaluation.

q: we introduce RefactorBench, a benchmark consisting of 100 large handcrafted multi-file refactoring tasks in popular open-source repositories.
r: EC6: refactoring benchmark, not building or extending an application from requirements, and main study is one agent (SWE-agent) with interface changes.
